page: Microsoft Azure E160ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz, providing 160 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 80 physical cores with symmetric multithreading. It features 1280 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside 9448 GB of bundled direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The processor incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16, while omitting dedicated hardware accelerators such as GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance in the top tier for compute and memory throughput. Multi-core performance metrics via stress-ng and PassMark show top-decile ratings, supported by large-block uncached memory read bandwidth of 462.59 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 210.18 GB/sec. Data processing tests show multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaching 1038.82 GB/sec. For database tasks, PassMark database operations and Redis SET operations (exceeding 202 million operations per second) reflect high transaction capacity under severe concurrency. CPU-driven inference benchmarks for small and medium language models also achieve high throughput, recording 371.42 tokens per second for prompt processing on a 7B parameter model.

The primary tradeoff of the E160ads_v7 involves architectural density and resource commitment. By pairing 160 vCPUs with 1.28 TB of memory and large NVMe disk arrays, the platform delivers high efficiency per node for clustered data systems that benefit from consolidating physical servers. However, systems that do not saturate its memory footprint or require GPU-specific vector processing will see diminishing returns from this configuration. The instance is well suited for large enterprise in-memory databases, distributed caching platforms such as Redis, enterprise analytics, high-volume transactional databases, and intensive extract-transform-load workloads.

Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V with an x86_64 architecture, it integrates instruction extensions like AVX-512 and AVX-512 VNNI without discrete GPU accelerators. Benchmarks position the instance in the top tier for multi-core compute, uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 462 GB/sec, and in-memory operations, including over 202 million Redis SET operations per second. It is tailored for demanding enterprise workloads such as in-memory databases, distributed caching layers, large-scale transaction processing, and data-intensive analytics pipelines.
